title: SkyTrace AI methodology (prototype, illustrative only)
summary: SkyTrace AI turns a last known position, ground speed, ground track and elapsed time into a straight-line baseline, a few deterministic heading-sensitivity scenarios, a buffered swept-sector region and a demo grid. It is a demonstration of geometry, not a search-planning model.

steps.name: Local projection
steps.detail: A per-request Azimuthal Equidistant (AEQD) projection on the WGS84 ellipsoid, centred on the last known position, units metres. Distance and azimuth from the centre are exact; shapes and areas far from the centre are approximate.

steps.name: Baseline
steps.detail: distance_nm = ground_speed_knots x elapsed_minutes / 60; east = d sin(h), north = d cos(h) (1 nm = 1852 m), inverse-projected to lon/lat. Cross-checked against pyproj Geod.fwd.

steps.name: Scenarios
steps.detail: Same distance along h-u and h+u, plus outer h-2u and h+2u (capped at 60 degrees), plus one optional hypothetical wind drift scenario that treats the speed as airspeed and adds wind speed x time toward (direction_from + 180). Offsets from the baseline use geodesic distances.

steps.name: Illustrative search region
steps.detail: Convex hull of the start, baseline and +/-u endpoints and arc points every ~5 degrees, buffered by max(position_uncertainty_nm, search_region_buffer_nm). Converted to GeoJSON [lon, lat], split at the antimeridian into a MultiPolygon if needed, exterior rings counter-clockwise.

steps.name: Demo grid
steps.detail: grid_size x grid_size cells over the region's projected bounding box. Score = Gaussian of the distance from cell centre to the baseline track segment (sigma = 0.25 x larger region extent), 0 outside the region, min-max normalised. Demonstration values only.

assumptions: The heading is interpreted as the ground track (direction of motion over the ground), because it is combined with ground speed. With wind present, true heading and ground track differ.
Straight-line motion at constant ground speed from the last known position for the whole elapsed time.
Ground speed already includes wind; wind is reported as context and never added to the baseline.
Heading sensitivity scenarios use fixed offsets of +/-u (and capped +/-2u) degrees; they are not measured errors.
Distances use the WGS84 ellipsoid; 1 nm = 1852 m exactly.
Geometry is built in a local azimuthal equidistant projection centred on the last known position.
Fuel and aircraft type are descriptive context and do not alter any geometry.
wind_limitations: Ground speed already includes the effect of wind, so wind is not applied to the baseline.
Separating wind from aircraft motion would require true airspeed and true heading, not ground speed.
Aircraft performance data (speeds, climb/descent, glide) is not modelled.
Altitude is unknown; wind varies strongly with altitude.
Winds are treated as constant; real winds vary in time and space.
Navigation mode (heading hold vs. track hold / autopilot) is unknown.
No track history (radar, ADS-B or other surveillance) is used.
fuel_limitations: Fuel percentage is reported only; endurance, range, reserves and consumption are not computed because usable capacity, fuel flow and aircraft performance data are not available.
limitations: No land/water mask, terrain, ocean drift, debris drift or survival modelling.
No turns, holding, descent profiles, glide range or ditching behaviour.
No surveillance data, track history or communication timelines.
Polar positions (|latitude| > 89) and regions reaching a pole are rejected.
Baseline distance is capped at 5000 nm.
Areas are approximate (AEQD is not equal-area).
disclaimer: SkyTrace AI is a hackathon PROTOTYPE for demonstration and education. It does not locate any real aircraft, does not compute operational search-and-rescue statistics, and must not be used for real search planning. All regions, scenarios and scores are illustrative sensitivity sketches based on simplified assumptions. Real incidents must be handled by the responsible Rescue Coordination Centre using approved tools.
